captions.text: ANTS Studio: from one demonstration to a robot program
captions.say: This is ANTS Studio. We start from one human demonstration of putting a bowl on a plate.
One command, policy-dev, starts the pipeline: Muse Wonder writes a program from the demonstration.

captions.text: Attempt 0: the first program fails in simulation
captions.say: The first program runs in the LIBERO simulator, and it fails.

captions.text: The model explains why it failed…
captions.say: The generator reads the rollout evidence and explains, in plain words, why it failed.

captions.text: …and rewrites the program. Every change is a readable diff
captions.say: Then it rewrites the program. Every change is a diff a person can read.

captions.text: Measured rollout evidence goes back as feedback
captions.say: What the simulator measured goes back to the model as feedback for the next attempt.

captions.text: Attempts 2 and 3 still fail; each repair builds on the last
captions.say: Attempts two and three still fail, and each repair builds on what the last one learned.
Attempt four passes. The task succeeds.

captions.text: Simulator keyframes of the passing rollout (seed 51)
captions.say: Here are the simulator keyframes of the passing rollout.

captions.text: Four repairs in one run. No training, only context
captions.say: Four repairs in one run. No weights were trained; only the context changed.
